title: Clean text and find the most frequent words
description:
Write two functions:

- `clean_text(text)` removes every character that isn't a letter or whitespace, then collapses repeated whitespace down to single spaces.
- `most_frequent_words(text, n)` cleans `text`, then returns the `n` most frequent words as `(count, word)` tuples, ties broken alphabetically.
examples:
sentence = '%I $am@% a %tea@cher%, &and&...'
clean_text(sentence)
-> 'I am a teacher and...'
most_frequent_words(clean_text(sentence), 3)
-> [(3, 'I'), (2, 'a'), (2, 'and')]

hints: Idea to consider: two regex substitutions - one to drop unwanted characters, one to collapse whitespace
re.sub(r'[^A-Za-z\s]', '', text) removes anything that isn't a letter or whitespace in one pass; re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', ...) afterward then collapses any resulting double spaces down to one.
clean_text does both substitutions in sequence and strips the result. most_frequent_words calls clean_text, splits on whitespace, counts with Counter, and returns the top n sorted by (-count, word).
expected_behavior: clean_text strips punctuation and normalizes whitespace; most_frequent_words returns the n most common words from the cleaned text.

hidden_tests.call: clean_text('%I $am@% a %tea@cher%, &and& I lo%#ve %tea@ching%;. There $is nothing; &as& mo@re rewarding as educa@ting &and& @emp%o@wering peo@ple. ;I found tea@ching m%o@re interesting tha@n any other %jo@bs. %Do@es thi%s mo@tivate yo@u to be a tea@cher!?')
hidden_tests.expected: 'I am a teacher and I love teaching There is nothing as more rewarding as educating and empowering people I found teaching more interesting than any other jobs Does this motivate you to be a teacher'
hidden_tests.label: source item 1, clean_text

hidden_tests.call: most_frequent_words('I am a teacher and I love teaching There is nothing as more rewarding as educating and empowering people I found teaching more interesting than any other jobs Does this motivate you to be a teacher', 3)

explanation: Two focused substitutions are easier to get right than one combined pattern: first strip everything that isn't a letter or whitespace, then separately clean up the whitespace that stripping left behind.
